newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL stocks sink over three pct on foreign sales.
newsitem.headline: KL stocks sink over three pct on foreign sales.

text.p: Kuala Lumpur blue chips sank over three percent as sales by foreigners knocked share prices deeper into the minus column in late morning, dealers said.
At 0302 GMT, the Composite Index of 100 leading stocks was down 35.33 points or 3.29 percent to 1,037.16, hitting a new year low.
One dealer said there was talk of a medium-sized foreign fund cashing out of Malaysian blue chips. "I think that's what's killing the market," he said.
"They say foreigners are dumping the market," said the head of research at a local firm. "But I don't know any particular reason," he added.
With the renewed downturn in the market, dealers said quality blue chips are looking increasingly attractive.
"It's a perfect buying opportunity," said Jonathan Duckett, an institutional dealer at Mohaiyani Securities. "Telekom hasn't been this low for two years."
At 0300 GMT, volume topped 67 million shares, and losers swamped gainers by 603 to 15.
